chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Muthanna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) disliked the picture in the houses.

key_terms.الصُّورَةَ: Picture or image (specifically of living beings in this context)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about pictures in the house?
ai.summary: This concise report from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) preference for modesty in domestic decor, reflecting the broader Shia jurisprudential discourse on 'taswir' (image-making) and its potential to lead to idolatry or vanity. While some scholars interpret this as a recommendation (karamah) rather than strict prohibition (haram), it underscores the ethical ideal of keeping living spaces free from distracting or pride-inducing representations of animate beings.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Musna,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that Ali<sup>asws</sup> disliked the pictures in the houses’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Muthanna’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Ali, Alayhi al-Salam, disliked the existence of pictures in houses.’”
